name: Tampines
summary: Mature east-region town with malls, parks, and MRT density — the self-contained heartland alternative when East Coast / Katong rents feel excessive.
body: Tampines is one of Singapore’s most complete new towns: town centre retail, strong bus/MRT links (East-West and Downtown Line stations), parks, and a predominantly local residential fabric. Forum neighbourhood threads treat it as the textbook “everything at the hub” east option — Our Tampines Hub / Century Square / IKEA shuttle culture — when Marine Parade condo premiums hurt and you accept a longer CBD hop. Expats shortlist it for space per dollar, airport-side logistics, and willingness to build social life outside lobby WhatsApp groups. Housing is HDB-heavy with suburban condo pockets; verify HDB rental eligibility before you fall in love with a specific block. Weekends skew toward town-centre malls and park connectors rather than Holland V brunch — which is either the point or the deal-breaker. Practical ops: Town Council bulky waste, chute fogging pest waves, laundry-pole etiquette, and OneService for dripping-clothes neighbours. Fibre is usually straightforward in mature HDB; still confirm TP release on handover week.
watchOuts: CBD commute longer than East Coast / Katong proper
Mall-centric weekends if that is not your taste
housingMix: Predominantly HDB with suburban condo options near town centre and park connectors.
commuteNotes: Tampines MRT (EWL) and Tampines West/East (DTL); buses across the east region; Changi Airport is a practical east advantage.
